chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Hassan, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked the insistence of people upon one another in asking (for favors), and He loved that for Himself; indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves to be asked and for what is with Him to be sought.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah love to be asked according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the divine etiquette of supplication by contrasting human social dynamics with God's unique attribute of generosity. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that Allah’s desire to be asked reflects His boundless mercy and readiness to grant, encouraging believers to approach Him with confident humility rather than the persistent pressure often seen in human interactions. This distinction reinforces the spiritual virtue of du'a as a direct channel for divine favor.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hajjal, from Hassan, from Abu Al Sabbah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Dislikes the people insisting before one another for help but He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves that for Himself<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> should be asked (from), and He<sup>azwj</sup> be sought for what is with Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hajjal from Hassan from abu al-Sabbah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, dislikes people insisting before one another for help but He likes it before Himself. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, loves that one begs and requests help from Him.”
